about: Curated key events of Swiss history for the year context drawer. Each event lists the title words used to find Federal Archives units that reference it (lower-case stems, German/French). Edited by hand; Apertus does not choose the events.

events.title: Federal Charter of 1291
events.summary: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden renew an alliance of mutual assistance; the charter was later treated as the founding document of the Confederation.

events.title: Battle of Morgarten
events.summary: Schwyz forces defeat a Habsburg army near Lake Ägeri.

events.title: Battle of Sempach
events.summary: The Confederates defeat Duke Leopold III of Austria, who dies in the battle.

events.title: Burgundian Wars: Grandson and Murten
events.summary: The Confederates defeat Charles the Bold of Burgundy at Grandson and Murten (1476) and at Nancy (1477).

events.title: Swabian War
events.summary: War against the Swabian League and Emperor Maximilian I; the Peace of Basel ends it.

events.title: Battle of Marignano
events.summary: Defeat by France near Milan; the Confederates withdraw from great-power politics in Italy.

events.title: Reformation in Zurich
events.summary: After the disputations of 1523 Zurich adopts Zwingli's Reformation; Bern, Basel and other places follow, and the Confederation splits by confession.

events.title: Second War of Kappel
events.summary: The Catholic cantons defeat Zurich; Zwingli is killed. The peace fixes the confessional balance for generations.

events.title: Peace of Westphalia
events.summary: The Confederation's exemption from the Holy Roman Empire is formally recognised.

events.title: Swiss Peasants' War
events.summary: Peasants of Lucerne, Bern, Solothurn and Basel rise against the city authorities and are defeated.

events.title: Toggenburg War (Second War of Villmergen)
events.summary: Zurich and Bern defeat the Catholic cantons; the Reformed side becomes dominant.

events.title: French invasion and Helvetic Republic
events.summary: France invades; the Old Confederation collapses and a centralised Helvetic Republic is proclaimed.

events.title: Stapfer-Enquête school survey
events.summary: Minister Philipp Albert Stapfer has every school in the Helvetic Republic describe its teacher, pupils and lessons: the first national school survey.

events.title: War of the Second Coalition in Switzerland; Suvorov crosses the Alps
events.summary: French, Austrian and Russian armies fight on Swiss soil (battles of Zurich); Suvorov's army crosses the Gotthard and the Panix pass.

events.title: Act of Mediation
events.summary: Napoleon imposes a federal constitution with 19 cantons, among them the new cantons of Aargau, St. Gallen, Graubünden, Thurgau, Ticino and Vaud.

events.title: Congress of Vienna and Federal Treaty
events.summary: The powers recognise Switzerland's perpetual neutrality; Valais, Neuchâtel and Geneva join; the Federal Treaty binds 22 cantons.

events.title: Year without a summer and famine
events.summary: After the Tambora eruption, cold and rain ruin harvests; famine and emigration follow, especially in eastern Switzerland.

events.title: Regeneration
events.summary: Liberal movements give many cantons new constitutions with popular sovereignty and freedom of the press.

events.title: Sonderbund and Sonderbund War
events.summary: Seven Catholic cantons form a separate alliance (1845); the federal army under General Dufour defeats it in November 1847 in a short civil war.

events.title: Federal Constitution: the federal state
events.summary: The Confederation becomes a federal state with a parliament of two chambers, the Federal Council and Bern as federal city.

events.title: The Swiss franc
events.summary: The federal coinage act replaces the cantonal currencies with the franc.

events.title: Federal Polytechnic School opens in Zurich
events.summary: The future ETH Zurich starts teaching.

events.title: Neuchâtel crisis
events.summary: A royalist uprising and the claims of the King of Prussia lead to a mobilisation; Prussia renounces Neuchâtel in 1857.

events.title: Red Cross and the first Geneva Convention
events.summary: Henry Dunant and others found the committee that becomes the ICRC (1863); the first Geneva Convention is signed (1864).

events.title: Revised Federal Constitution
events.summary: The total revision strengthens the Confederation and introduces the optional referendum.

events.title: Gotthard railway opens
events.summary: The Gotthard tunnel (bored 1872–1880) links northern Switzerland and Ticino by rail.

events.title: Popular initiative and the first national day
events.summary: The popular initiative for partial revisions of the constitution is introduced; the 600th anniversary of the Confederation is celebrated on 1 August for the first time.

events.title: Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) start operating
events.summary: After the 1898 nationalisation vote, the main private railways are taken over by the Confederation.

events.title: Simplon tunnel opens
events.summary: The rail tunnel between Brig and Domodossola opens.

events.title: First World War: active service
events.summary: The army guards the borders under General Wille; food and fuel become scarce and social tensions grow.

events.title: General strike and Spanish flu
events.summary: The national general strike of 12–14 November is ended by the army; the influenza pandemic kills about 25,000 people in Switzerland (1918–1919).

events.title: First National Council election by proportional representation
events.summary: Proportional representation, accepted in 1918, ends the absolute majority of the Free Democrats.

events.title: Switzerland joins the League of Nations
events.summary: Voters accept membership; Geneva becomes the League's seat.

events.title: National Exhibition in Zurich (Landi)
events.summary: The national exhibition becomes a symbol of 'spiritual national defence' on the eve of the war.

events.title: Second World War: active service
events.summary: General Guisan commands the army; the Rütli report (1940) and the Alpine redoubt; rationing, refugees turned back at the border.

events.title: Old-age and survivors' insurance (AHV/AVS)
events.summary: Voters accept the federal pension insurance in 1947; it pays out from 1948.

events.title: Refugees from Hungary
events.summary: After the Soviet suppression of the uprising, Switzerland takes in about 14,000 Hungarian refugees.

events.title: The 'magic formula'
events.summary: The four largest parties share the seven Federal Council seats (2-2-2-1), a formula kept until 2003.

events.title: National Exhibition in Lausanne (Expo 64)
events.summary: The national exhibition in Lausanne.

events.title: Women's right to vote
events.summary: On 7 February 1971 men vote to give women the vote and the right to stand at the federal level.

events.title: Canton of Jura
events.summary: Voters accept the new canton in 1978; it becomes the 26th canton on 1 January 1979.

events.title: Youth unrest in Zurich
events.summary: Protests for an autonomous youth centre start at the Zurich opera house and spread to other cities.

events.title: Schweizerhalle chemical fire
events.summary: A warehouse fire near Basel on 1 November pollutes the Rhine with chemicals.

events.title: Secret files scandal (Fichenaffäre)
events.summary: A parliamentary inquiry reveals that the federal police kept files on some 900,000 people and organisations.

events.title: No to the European Economic Area
events.summary: On 6 December voters and cantons reject joining the EEA.

events.title: Swissair grounding
events.summary: The national airline grounds its fleet on 2 October and is wound up.

events.title: Switzerland joins the United Nations
events.summary: Voters accept UN membership on 3 March; Switzerland joins in September.

events.title: Gotthard Base Tunnel opens
events.summary: The 57 km rail tunnel, the core of the NEAT project, opens on 1 June.
